# 404 (page not found) page

What a page-not-found response must do so people and search engines are not stranded or misled.

Use when: Any site, before launch and after a relaunch or URL change.

Updated 2026-11-25. 14 items, checked by hand. Record each item on its own row as passed, failed, skipped (with the reason) or unavailable (with what would settle it), and no other word. No score. An item whose heading ends "Pro checks this automatically" keeps that note on its own row; the other items do not get it.

## 404-01 · critical · Pro checks this automatically

An address that does not exist returns HTTP status 404, or 410 for content removed on purpose.

- Check: Request a made-up address on the live or preview site, for example /this-page-does-not-exist-check, and read the status code.
- Pass: Status 404 or 410. Not 200 (a soft 404), and not a redirect to the home page.
- Sources: [Google Search Central: HTTP status codes and soft 404 errors](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/http-network-errors)
- Sitewright (Pro, in fkweb-dev-pro) checks this automatically.

## 404-02 · warning · Pro checks this automatically

The site serves its own page-not-found page, not the host's or framework's default.

- Check: Look for a 404 page in the build and open the made-up address in a browser.
- Pass: A designed page in the site's own template is shown.
- Sources: [GOV.UK Design System: page not found pages](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/patterns/page-not-found-pages/); [Nielsen Norman Group: improving the dreaded 404 error message](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/improving-dreaded-404-error-message/)
- Sitewright (Pro, in fkweb-dev-pro) checks this automatically.

## 404-03 · warning

The main heading says in plain words that the page cannot be found.

- Check: Read the h1 of the 404 page.
- Pass: A plain heading such as "Page not found". A bare "Error 404" or a joke alone fails.
- Sources: [GOV.UK Design System: page not found pages](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/patterns/page-not-found-pages/); [Nielsen Norman Group: improving the dreaded 404 error message](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/improving-dreaded-404-error-message/)

## 404-04 · info

The text gives the likely reasons briefly, without blaming the reader.

- Check: Read the body text.
- Pass: One or two short lines (mistyped address, moved or removed page), with no wording that blames the reader.
- Sources: [GOV.UK Design System: page not found pages](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/patterns/page-not-found-pages/); [Nielsen Norman Group: improving the dreaded 404 error message](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/improving-dreaded-404-error-message/)

## 404-05 · warning

The page offers a way forward: a link to the home page and to search or the main sections.

- Check: Open the page at 320 px and 1280 px wide and look for the links.
- Pass: A home link plus either a search box or links to the main sections, visible without scrolling at 320 px.
- Sources: [Nielsen Norman Group: improving the dreaded 404 error message](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/improving-dreaded-404-error-message/); [Nielsen Norman Group: 10 usability heuristics for user interface design](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/ten-usability-heuristics/)

## 404-06 · warning · Pro checks this automatically

The usual header navigation and footer are present, as on every other page.

- Check: Compare the 404 page with any content page.
- Pass: Same header navigation and footer as the rest of the site.
- Sources: [WCAG 2.2, 3.2.3 Consistent Navigation](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/consistent-navigation); [Nielsen Norman Group: improving the dreaded 404 error message](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/improving-dreaded-404-error-message/)
- Sitewright (Pro, in fkweb-dev-pro) checks this automatically.

## 404-07 · info

People who expected something here can reach a contact route.

- Check: Look for a link to the contact page or a contact address.
- Pass: A contact link or address is on the page or in its footer.
- Sources: [GOV.UK Design System: page not found pages](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/patterns/page-not-found-pages/); [WCAG 2.2, 3.2.6 Consistent Help](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/consistent-help)

## 404-08 · info · Pro checks this automatically

The page title says the page was not found and names the site.

- Check: Read the title element.
- Pass: A title such as "Page not found – Site name".
- Sources: [WCAG 2.2, 2.4.2 Page Titled](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/page-titled)
- Sitewright (Pro, in fkweb-dev-pro) checks this automatically.

## 404-09 · warning · Pro checks this automatically

The 404 page is not listed in the XML sitemap.

- Check: Search the sitemap for the 404 page's address.
- Pass: Not listed.
- Sources: [Google Search Central: HTTP status codes and soft 404 errors](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/http-network-errors)
- Sitewright (Pro, in fkweb-dev-pro) checks this automatically.

## 404-10 · warning · Pro checks this automatically

Internal links do not lead to missing pages.

- Check: Run an internal link check over the site, and look at the Not found rows in Search Console's Page indexing report where it is available.
- Pass: No internal link returns 404. Any 404s Search Console reports are either fixed or deliberate.
- Sources: [Search Console Help: Page indexing report](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/7440203)
- Sitewright (Pro, in fkweb-dev-pro) checks this automatically.

## 404-11 · critical · Pro checks this automatically

After a relaunch or URL change, every old address that had a replacement redirects to it with a permanent (301 or 308) redirect.

- Check: Compare a list of the old site's addresses with the new redirect map, and request a sample of old addresses.
- Pass: Each old address with a new equivalent ends at that page in one permanent redirect. Only addresses with no equivalent return 404 or 410.
- Sources: [Google Search Central: site moves with URL changes](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/site-move-with-url-changes)
- Sitewright (Pro, in fkweb-dev-pro) checks this automatically.

## 404-12 · warning · Pro checks this automatically

The page has one h1, landmarks, a page language, and links whose text says where they go.

- Check: Run the accessibility checks on the 404 page.
- Pass: One h1, header, main and footer landmarks, a lang attribute, and no link text such as "click here".
- Sources: [WCAG 2.2, 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/link-purpose-in-context); [WCAG 2.2, 1.3.1 Info and Relationships](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/info-and-relationships)
- Sitewright (Pro, in fkweb-dev-pro) checks this automatically.

## 404-13 · info · Pro checks this automatically

The message and links show without JavaScript.

- Check: Load the 404 page with JavaScript turned off.
- Pass: The heading, text and links are visible.
- Sources: [Google Search Central: JavaScript SEO basics](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/javascript-seo-basics)
- Sitewright (Pro, in fkweb-dev-pro) checks this automatically.

## 404-14 · info · Pro checks this automatically

The wording sounds like the rest of the site, with no stock phrases.

- Check: Read it next to another page of the site.
- Pass: Same voice as the site. No stock lines such as "Oops, looks like you're lost in space".
- Sources: fkweb-dev house rule: no generic AI-look tells (stock phrases, identical icon cards, vague adjectives); [Nielsen Norman Group: improving the dreaded 404 error message](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/improving-dreaded-404-error-message/)
- Sitewright (Pro, in fkweb-dev-pro) checks this automatically.
